correctness.rationale: For positives P, contract their components and treat negative edges as incompatibility constraints; a labeled trace is realizable with exactly q blocks iff quotient chromatic number <=q<=number of contracted components. Forest S avoids positive-induced negative loops/cycles for every split and has at most n-q edges, proving sufficiency; a cycle with one negative edge and the all-positive component count prove necessity. Graphic-matroid truncation and forest-Tutte expansion follow; q=3 arbitrary negative trace is NP-complete by 3-colorability. All n,q boundary conventions are consistent. Independent exhaustive small-n support checks passed 4306 cases. Universal proof not inferred from enumeration.

originality.rationale: FAIL: the earlier November 2 published refinement-closed partition support theorem establishes for all families closed under splitting that shattering is forest plus feasible component partition. Specialize it to partitions with AT LEAST q blocks: feasibility is n-|S|>=q. For any forest S satisfying this, every realizable positive/negative assignment in this >=q class can also be realized with EXACTLY q blocks: contracted negative edges form a forest, admit a proper 2-coloring (q>=2), and color splitting reaches every exact count through c_P. Thus the claimed exact-q support/VC/graphic-matroid theorem follows from the earlier broader theorem with this elementary quotient coloring step. The standalone trace-coloring criterion and its 3-color hardness are direct textbook graph coloring; enumeration is standard Tutte/Cayley. No new valuable remainder is isolated.
residual_risks: This is a decisive earlier-theorem implication, not merely failure to find a novel result; no independent corrected claim was staged.
The prior refinement-closed theorem is mathematically broader but not literally the exact-q class; the forest-to-exact-q reduction was checked explicitly.
Finite exhaustive 4306 support cases do not establish science novelty.
